questions.question: Select the most appropriate option that can substitute the underlined segment in the given sentence. I found my teacher’s points casual and informal in the group discussion.
questions.questionHtml:
Select the most appropriate option that can substitute the underlined segment in the given sentence.

I found my teacher’s points casual and informal in the group discussion.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is: Option 2 i.e. free and easy.

Key Points

  • The word "casual and informal" means something that is relaxed and friendly, without much formality or strictness. (आरामदेह और अनौपचारिक)
    • Example: His casual and informal approach made the meeting more comfortable for everyone.
  • "Free and easy" refers to something that is natural, relaxed, and not restricted by strict rules or formality. (स्वच्छंद और आरामदेह)
    • Example: Her free and easy demeanor made her very approachable.
  • Hence, we can infer that the phrase 'free and easy' aptly substitutes 'casual and informal' in this context.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 2 i.e. free and easy.

Additional Information

Here are the other options explained along with their Hindi meanings and example sentences:

  • Flesh and blood (मांस और रक्त): Refers to human beings, especially in the context of family or kinship.
    • Example: Despite their disagreements, they are still flesh and blood and care for each other.
  • Foot the bill (खर्च उठाना): To pay the bill for something, especially when it is considered expensive.
    • Example: The company will foot the bill for the team’s travel expenses.
  • Fair and square (निष्पक्ष और ईमानदारी से): In an honest and straightforward manner.
    • Example: He won the competition fair and square, without any cheating.

questions.question: Select the most appropriate option that can substitute the underlined segment in the given sentence. Little that I knew of the English language was not sufficient to make me an English teacher.

questions.solution:

questions.question: Directions: Select the option that will improve the underlined part of the given sentence. In case no improvement is needed select 'No improvement required.' He fell over in studies owing to his illness.
questions.questionHtml:
Directions: Select the option that will improve the underlined part of the given sentence. In case no improvement is needed select 'No improvement required.'

He fell over in studies owing to his illness.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is 'fell behind.'

Key Points

  • In the underlined segment, the phrasal verb ''fell over'' is incorrect.
  • The given sentence is talking about a student who failed to keep up with his studies due to illness.
  • The phrasal verb ''fell over'' means (of a person) losing one's balance and collapse.
  • Therefore, the phrasal verb ''fell behind'' should be used in place of the phrasal verb ''fell over''.
  • The phrasal verb ''fell behind'' means to fail to do something fast enough or on time.
     

Hence, the correct answer is option 3.

Correct Sentence: He fell behind in studies owing to his illness.

Additional Information 

  • ''Fell out'' means to argue with someone and stop being friends with them. (''Fell out'' का अर्थ है किसी से बहस करना और उससे दोस्ती करना बंद कर देना)
  • ''Fell for'' means to be very attracted to someone and to start to love them. (''Fell for'' का अर्थ है किसी के प्रति बहुत आकर्षित होना और उससे प्यार करना शुरू करना)
     

Hinglish

  • दिए गए रेखांकित खण्ड में phrasal verb ''fell over'' गलत है।
  • दिया गया वाक्य एक छात्र के बारे में बात कर रहा है जो बीमारी के कारण अपनी पढ़ाई में असफल रहा।
  • Phrasal verb ''fell over'' का अर्थ है किसी व्यक्ति का अपना संतुलन खोना और गिरना।
  • इसलिए, phrasal verb ''fell over'' के स्थान पर phrasal verb ''fell behind'' का प्रयोग किया जाना चाहिए।
  • Phrasal verb ''fell behind'' का अर्थ है पर्याप्त तेजी से या समय पर कुछ करने में असफल होना।
     

अत: सही उत्तर विकल्प 3 है।

सही वाक्य: He fell behind in studies owing to his illness.

questions.question: Select the most appropriate option to substitute the underlined segment in the given sentence. Transnational linkages, for example, sever the nation-state's integrity and corrupt state-society relations.
questions.questionHtml:
Select the most appropriate option to substitute the underlined segment in the given sentence.
Transnational linkages, for example, sever the nation-state's integrity and corrupt state-society relations.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is: Option 1 i.e. cohesion and erode.

Key Points

  • "Cohesion" refers to the action or fact of forming a united whole. (संबद्धता)
    • Example: The cohesion among the team members was evident in their smooth coordination during the project.
  • The word "erode" means to gradually wear away or be worn away by natural agents. (क्षरण करना)
    • Example: The coastline has been eroded by the sea.

Therefore, the correct answer is: cohesion and erode.

Additional Information

Here are the other options explained along with their Hindi meanings and example sentences:

  • Divergence (विचलन): The process or state of diverging.
    • Example: There was a clear divergence between the two opinions.
  • Relativity (सापेक्षता): The absence of standards of absolute and universal application.
    • Example: The theory of relativity revolutionized physics.
  • Severance (विच्छेद): The action of ending a connection or relationship.
    • Example: The severance of diplomatic ties was a significant event.
  • Revolution (क्रांति): A forcible overthrow of a government or social order, in favor of a new system.
    • Example: The Industrial Revolution brought great changes to society.
  • Controversy (विवाद): Disagreement, typically when prolonged, public, and heated.
    • Example: The new policy caused a lot of controversy.
  • Diminution (कमी): A reduction in the size, extent, or importance of something.
    • Example: There has been a diminution in the number of students attending the school.

questions.question: Select the most appropriate ANTONYM of the highlighted word in the given sentence. The author\'s writing style is characterised by a subtle and nuanced use of language.

  • The phrase "springs to mind" refers to the sudden occurrence or the arrival of a thought or idea in one's mind ("मन में आना" or "अचानक ख्याल आना").
    • Example: While trying to think of a solution, an innovative idea suddenly springs to mind.
  • The correct phrase "dawns on" similarly means to become apparent or to come to someone's understanding suddenly ("समझ में आना" or "अचानक एहसास होना").
  • Hence, the correct substitution is dawns on.
Therefore, the correct answer is 'Option 3'.
 
Additional Information
  • "Almost always" implies something happening very frequently ("लगभग हमेशा").
  • "Forget about something" denotes the act of failing to remember something ("किसी चीज को भूल जाना").
  • "From the beginning of time" signifies something happening since the very start or for a very long period ("आदि काल से").

questions.question: Replace the bracketed word with one of the given options, which suitably replaces the word without changing the meaning of the sentence: There are several ways to (mitigate) a blowout without losing control or playing soft.
questions.questionHtml:
Replace the bracketed word with one of the given options, which suitably replaces the word without changing the meaning of the sentence:

There are several ways to (mitigate) a blowout without losing control or playing soft.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is: Option 2.

Key Points 

  • Mitigate means to make something less severe, serious, or painful; to alleviate. (कम करना)
    • Example: The government took steps to mitigate the impact of the financial crisis.
  • Allay means to diminish or put at rest (fear, suspicion, or worry). (शांत करना)
    • Example: The company's CEO spoke to allay the concerns of investors.
  • Therefore, the correct answer is: allay.

Additional Information

Here are the other options explained along with their Hindi meanings:

  • Spread (फैलाना): extend over a large or increasing area.
    • Example: The news of the discovery spread quickly.
  • Aggravate (बिगाड़ना): make (a problem, injury, or offense) worse or more serious.
    • Example: Scratching the rash will only aggravate it.
  • Intensify (तीव्र करना): to make more intense.
    • Example: The conflict intensified after the declaration.

I picked up my little clock and it began to dance gracefully.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is '3' i.e. chime prettily.

Key Points

  • The phrase "chime prettily" is appropriate because it describes the sound a clock makes when it functions, which fits the context of picking up the clock and it beginning to work.
  • The other options do not convey the intended meaning:

Hence, the correct answer is option 3.

questions.question: Improve the underlined part of the sentence. Choose 'No improvement' as an answer if the sentence is grammatically correct. Walking through the dew , he wet his sneakers.
questions.questionHtml:
Improve the underlined part of the sentence. Choose 'No improvement' as an answer if the sentence is grammatically correct.

Walking through the dew, he wet his sneakers.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is: Option 1.

Key Points

  • The word "through" means moving in one side and out of the other side of (an opening, channel, or location). (के माध्यम से)
    • Example: We walked through the forest to get to the lake.
  • "Dew" refers to tiny drops of water that form on cool surfaces at night, when atmospheric vapor condenses. (ओस)
    • Example: In the morning, the grass was covered with dew.
  • Hence, we can infer that the original sentence is grammatically correct and does not need any improvement.

Therefore, the correct answer is: No improvement.

Additional Information

Here are the other options explained along with their Hindi meanings and example sentences:

  • From the dew (ओस से): This phrase suggests a source, but it doesn't fit well in the context of the sentence.
    • Example: He collected water from the dew on the leaves.
  • Through the dewy (ओस भरी): This is incorrect because "dewy" is an adjective and should describe a noun.
    • Example: The dewy grass sparkled in the morning light.
  • Across the dewy (ओस भरे पर): This is incorrect because "dewy" is an adjective and should describe a noun.
    • Example: She walked across the dewy meadow.
